title: Deliverance from Sin’s Power
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Deliverance from sin’s power means that salvation breaks sin’s ruling mastery over the believer. Christians still battle sin, but they are no longer slaves under its dominion.
summary: Deliverance from sin’s power means that salvation breaks sin’s ruling mastery over the believer. Christians still battle sin, but they are no longer slaves under its dominion.
christFocus: Jesus Christ delivers His people from the dominion of sin by His death and resurrection. In Him, believers are freed to live under grace and offer themselves to God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin is not only guilt; it is also bondage. Apart from grace, sinners are enslaved to sin’s rule and cannot free themselves by willpower alone.

Through union with Christ, believers have died to sin’s mastery and are alive to God. Sin remains a real enemy, but it is no longer the believer’s rightful lord.

Deliverance does not mean temptation disappears or growth becomes easy. It means the believer fights from a new position: under grace, indwelt by the Spirit, and belonging to Christ.

Christ frees His people for holiness. Salvation delivers from lawlessness and creates a people zealous for good works, not a people content to remain mastered by sin.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
This doctrine speaks directly to bondage, addiction, compulsive sin, and patterns that feel impossible to break. The Gospel offers more than forgiveness after failure; it announces freedom from sin’s dominion.

It also guards against despair. A believer may still struggle deeply, but struggle is not the same as slavery. Christ has the final claim over His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Fight sin as one who belongs to Christ. Do not say, “This is just who I am,” when Jesus has broken sin’s mastery. Use the means of grace, walk by the Spirit, confess honestly, seek help wisely, and present yourself to God for obedience.
